summary: Paul F. Knitter worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1962–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1968–1972), later holding a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq was a historian who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Voskenslaan, Ghent University, and the University of Liège (~1868–1875). He was a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University (from 1883), where he became Rektor in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Paul Dundas and Rupert Gethin, completing a PhD at the University of Bristol. He held a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan Collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and later at Columbia University in Buddhist studies (2003) and Classical Tibetan (2016).

Paul Groner specialized in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a PhD from Yale University and studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa (1971–1974), later serving as professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

Paul Hacker was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Frankfurt, Heidelberg, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Bonn (1949, 1955–1963 chair) and Münster (1950, 1963–1978 head of Indian Studies).

Paul Harrison works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Auckland (MA 1970–1976) and the Australian National University (PhD ~1974–1979 under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana), later holding posts at Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford.
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Kanazawa University, attested in 1991 as a lecturer and again in 2002.

Paul J. Griffiths studied at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and earned a PhD from UW–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he held chairs at the University of Illinois Chicago (2000–2007) and Duke University (~2007–2017).
Paul K. Nietupski works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Kingsbury worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).
Paul Kiparsky is a linguist and Indologist who studied at King Edward's School and completed his studies at MIT under Morris Halle (~1962–1965). He held a post at Stanford University (~1984).

Paul L. Swanson specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UW–Madison under Minoru Kiyota (attested 1985), later becoming a professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He served as director at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Mus studied at EPHE, INALCO, Oxford, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at EFEO (1927–1940), EPHE (1937), Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University (1951).
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1881–1887). He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1894–1928).

Paul Pelliot studied in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. An expert in Sinology, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, he taught at EFEO (1900) and held the Central Asian chair at Collège de France (1911–1945).
Paul R. Brass was a scholar of Indology who studied at Harvard College, the University of Chicago, and Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of Washington (~1967–2002).
Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1876). He subsequently held a post at the University of Lyon (~1879–1908).

Paul Ricœur studied at Rennes and the University of Paris. A philosopher, his primary appointments included the University of Strasbourg (1948–1956), the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1956–1965), Paris Nanterre (1964–1970), and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).
